$comment: API-path ownership contract, enforced by scripts/check-route-ownership.mjs.
The ingress splits /api across several services by LONGEST-PREFIX match:
`/api/apps` goes to fuzefront-applications while the remaining `/api` goes to
fuzefront-backend. A route can therefore be fully implemented, unit-tested and
green in CI while being a 404 in every deployed environment, because it was
mounted on a service that does not own its path prefix. That is exactly what
happened to the app-installation endpoints: implemented on the backend, owned
by applications-service, 404 in prod, and no test could see it because unit
tests mount routers directly and never traverse the ingress.
Each entry pins three things that must agree:
path          - an API path the frontend actually calls
servedBy      - the k8s Service the chart's ingress resolves that path to
implementedIn - the router source file that must implement it
mountedIn     - the service entrypoint that must mount that router
